items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Aaron Smith and I became quite friendly, and we used to have a few drinks together in the Turf bar

ctx.x: The only musicians in the band other than Sy that I had known before were Dickie and Henry Wells, Eddie Barefield, Lamar Wright,Sr., George Dorsey, Billie Kyle and Wallace Bishop. I had seen Freddie Williams but did not know him very well. Aaron Smith and I became quite friendly, and we used to have a few drinks together in the Turf bar which was down stairs under the Zanzibar, when we had our intermission. Sometimes we went to Beafsteak Charlie's on 50th Street near Broadway, where many musicians hung out.

One night I told Smittie as most everyone called Aaron, that I had been in Europe during a certain time and had recorded with a guitarist named Django Reinhardt and I was surprised when he told me that he knew of Django and considered him the greatest improvising guitarist that ever lived.

A real genius, which he was. From that night on, Smittie began to call me "Mighty" and I suppose it was because he appreciated the fact that I had been fortunate enough and capable of recording with such a great musician as Django.
